newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS -New issues rescue dull session.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS -New issues rescue dull session.

text.p: The absence of U.S. economic data, a lack of retail activity and warm temperatures all served to dampen trading activity in the corporate bond secondary arena on Wednesday, players said.
"It's been deadsville today," said one industrials trader in response to Wednesday's session.
Another trader echoed this view, "We really didn't see any retail bids come in ... our market was so quiet I was able to get out for lunch today and take in some sun."
The bulk of Wednesday's action took place in the primary sector where approximately $2.2 billion in new debt priced.
About $1.2 billion in new investment-grade debt was priced in the public market on Wednesday and another $1.0 billion in the private placement arena, dealers said.

Among investment-grade offerings was Potash Corp of Saskatchewan, a Canadian-based firm in the integrated fertilizer business. The company sold $400 million in 7.125 percent 10-year notes at 67 basis points over Treasuries via lead underwriter Smith Barney, dealers said.
Another $300 million in debentures was sold by Tenneco Inc via lead manager Credit Suisse First Boston.
The deal consisted of 7.125 percent 20-year debentures which were priced to yield a spread of 77 basis points over Treasuries.

In addition, Mercantile Bancorp sold $200 million in 7.30 percent 10-year notes at 75 basis points, $150 million in 6.80 percent four-year notes at 43 basis points and $150 million in 7.05 percent seven-year notes at 57 basis points, said lead manager Salomon Brothers Inc.
Seperately, among high-yield private-placement issues, Jacor Communications set $150 milllion in 8.75 percent 10-year 144A notes at 220 basis points over Treasuries.
Another $200 million was brought by Pioneer Americas Acquisition Corp, a Houston-based manufacturer and distributor of specialty chemicals.
The deal consisted of 9.25 percent 10-year notes whcih priced at a spread of 271 basis points over Treasuries, sources said.
In addition, soft drinks producer, Cott Corp, sold $125 million in 8.50 percent 10-year notes at 196 basis points over Treasuries. The deal was underwritten by Morgan Stanley & Co Inc.

Centerior Energy also tapped the market with a three-part debt offering. The firms sold $200 million in 7.30 percent 10-year notes at 75 basis points, $150 million 6.80 percent four-year notes at 43 basis points and $150 million in 7.05 percent seven-year notes at 57 basis points over Treasuries.
Secondary high-yield prices ended on a firm note in very light trading volume as most players focused on the downpour of new issues hitting the market.
In the government market, the benchmark U.S. Treasury 30-year bond closed unchanged at 97-8/32 to yield 6.84 percent.
